title: Co-projection compatibility with normalized etale exceptional pullback
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [sk-def-purity-conv], with $A=A_{E,n}$, and work in the bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale categories with the operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $e:U\to X$ be a separated finite-type étale morphism, and put $V=Z\times_XU$ with maps $v:V\to Z$ and $i_U:V\hookrightarrow U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], $v$ is étale. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] and let $L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ be tensor-invertible; the exceptional inverse images preserve the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], so $Ri^!K$, $Re^!K$ and $K\otimes^LL$ again lie in them. Use the normalized comparisons $\rho_e:Re^!\simeq Le^*$ and $\rho_v:Rv^!\simeq Lv^*$ of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization], and the canonical exceptional composition comparisons $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\simeq Rf^!Rg^!$ of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition]. Define the comparison by the explicit five-arrow pasting
$$B_{e,i,K}:Ri_U^!Le^*K\xrightarrow{Ri_U^!(\rho_{e,K}^{-1})}Ri_U^!Re^!K\xrightarrow{c_{e,i_U,K}^{-1}}R(ei_U)^!K=R(iv)^!K\xrightarrow{c_{i,v,K}}Rv^!Ri^!K\xrightarrow{\rho_{v,Ri^!K}}Lv^*Ri^!K.$$ 
Then the canonical co-projection isomorphisms of [lem-pur-coprojection] form a commutative square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Ri_U^!\bigl(Le^*(K\otimes^L L)\bigr)&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coProj}_{i_U}}&Ri_U^!Le^*K\otimes^L Li_U^*Le^*L\\
\downarrow B_{e,i,K\otimes L}&&\downarrow B_{e,i,K}\otimes\mathrm{can}\\
Lv^*Ri^!(K\otimes^L L)&\xrightarrow{\,Lv^*\operatorname{coProj}_{i}}&Lv^*Ri^!K\otimes^L Lv^*Li^*L,
\end{array}
$$
where $\mathrm{can}:Li_U^*Le^*L\simeq Lv^*Li^*L$ is the canonical pullback-composition identification, the top arrow is preceded by $Ri_U^!$ of the tensor-pullback comparison $Le^*(K\otimes^LL)\simeq Le^*K\otimes^LLe^*L$, and the bottom arrow is followed by $Lv^*(Ri^!K\otimes^LLi^*L)\simeq Lv^*Ri^!K\otimes^LLv^*Li^*L$. In particular, the co-projection isomorphism for a Tate twist and shift commutes with replacing each etale exceptional inverse image by its normalized ordinary pullback comparison.

source.place: Step 4(ii), etale-local comparison paragraph: compatibility of the co-projection maps for Tate shifts with the normalized etale identifications

proof.text: The fibre product square has $v:V\to Z$ etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and $v$, $i_U$ are separated of finite type as base changes. By the domain and preservation hypotheses included in the statement, every displayed object is in $D^b_{ctf}$, the domain of the chosen comparisons. The maps $c_{e,i_U}$ and $c_{i,v}$ are the specified exceptional-composition comparisons of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition]; they are isomorphisms, being by [lem-sf-mate] the mates of the compact-support compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. With $\rho_e,\rho_v$ invertible [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization], the five-arrow composite $B_{e,i,K}$ is a well-defined isomorphism, natural in $K$.

source.place: Step 4(ii), etale-local comparison paragraph: the normalized exceptional composition pasting

proof.text: Apply the canonical co-projection statement [lem-pur-coprojection] to $i_U$ with the objects $Le^*K$ and the invertible $Le^*L$, and to $i$ with $K$ and $L$. By its construction, each co-projection is the comparison of right adjoints induced by the projection isomorphism of the specified projection transformation [def-exchange-projection] with an inverse of the twist object; unwinding the adjunctions, it is the inverse of the map $\kappa_{i_U,Le^*K,Le^*L}$, resp. $\kappa_{i,K,L}$, defined in [lem-pur-coprojection-composition-mate] (whose statement records this). So the square to be proved is equivalent to the equality, of maps $Ri_U^!Le^*K\otimes^LLi_U^*Le^*L\to Lv^*Ri^!(K\otimes^LL)$, $$B_{e,i,K\otimes L}\circ Ri_U^!(\mu_e^{-1})\circ\kappa_{i_U,Le^*K,Le^*L}=Lv^*(\kappa_{i,K,L})\circ\mu_v^{-1}\circ(B_{e,i,K}\otimes\mathrm{can}),\qquad(*)$$ with $\mu_e,\mu_v$ the tensor-pullback comparisons in the statement; the right vertical arrow uses exactly $B_{e,i,K}$ tensored with $\mathrm{can}$.

source.place: Step 4(ii), etale-local comparison paragraph: the co-projection factors

proof.text: Compute the left side of $(*)$. By [lem-pur-etale-rho-monoidal-mate] for $e$, $\rho_{e,K\otimes L}^{-1}\mu_e^{-1}=\kappa_{e,K,L}(\rho_{e,K}^{-1}\otimes1)$, so $Ri_U^!(\rho_{e,K\otimes L}^{-1}\mu_e^{-1})\kappa_{i_U,Le^*K,Le^*L}=Ri_U^!(\kappa_{e,K,L})\,\kappa_{i_U,Re^!K,Le^*L}\,(Ri_U^!\rho_{e,K}^{-1}\otimes1)$, the last by naturality of $\kappa_{i_U}$ in its first argument (it is defined from natural transformations). By [lem-pur-coprojection-composition-mate] for $(g,f)=(e,i_U)$, $Ri_U^!(\kappa_{e,K,L})\kappa_{i_U,Re^!K,Le^*L}=c_{e,i_U,K\otimes L}\,\kappa_{ei_U,K,L}\,(c_{e,i_U,K}^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{can}_1^{-1})$ with $\mathrm{can}_1:L(ei_U)^*L\simeq Li_U^*Le^*L$. Since $ei_U=iv$ as morphisms $V\to X$, $\kappa_{ei_U}=\kappa_{iv}$, and [lem-pur-coprojection-composition-mate] for $(g,f)=(i,v)$ gives $c_{i,v,K\otimes L}\kappa_{iv,K,L}=Rv^!(\kappa_{i,K,L})\,\kappa_{v,Ri^!K,Li^*L}\,(c_{i,v,K}\otimes\mathrm{can}_2)$ with $\mathrm{can}_2:L(iv)^*L\simeq Lv^*Li^*L$. Hence the left side of $(*)$ equals $\rho_{v,Ri^!(K\otimes L)}Rv^!(\kappa_{i,K,L})\,\kappa_{v,Ri^!K,Li^*L}\,\bigl(c_{i,v,K}c_{e,i_U,K}^{-1}Ri_U^!(\rho_{e,K}^{-1})\otimes\mathrm{can}_2\mathrm{can}_1^{-1}\bigr)$. By naturality of $\rho_v$ [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization], $\rho_vRv^!(\kappa_i)=Lv^*(\kappa_i)\rho_v$, and by [lem-pur-etale-rho-monoidal-mate] for the etale map $v$ (separated of finite type, $v$ etale by step 1), $\rho_{v,Ri^!K\otimes Li^*L}\kappa_{v,Ri^!K,Li^*L}=\mu_v^{-1}(\rho_{v,Ri^!K}\otimes1)$. Substituting, the left side becomes $Lv^*(\kappa_{i,K,L})\mu_v^{-1}\bigl(\rho_{v,Ri^!K}c_{i,v,K}c_{e,i_U,K}^{-1}Ri_U^!(\rho_{e,K}^{-1})\otimes\mathrm{can}_2\mathrm{can}_1^{-1}\bigr)=Lv^*(\kappa_{i,K,L})\mu_v^{-1}(B_{e,i,K}\otimes\mathrm{can})$, because $\mathrm{can}_2\mathrm{can}_1^{-1}$ is the canonical identification $Li_U^*Le^*L\simeq Lv^*Li^*L$ (both are the pullback-composition isomorphisms fixed in the statement, for the same composite $ei_U=iv$, so the composite is by definition the identification $\mathrm{can}$ of the statement). This is the right side of $(*)$. No base-change exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ enters: every factor of $B$ is a composition comparison or a normalized $\rho$.

source.place: Step 4(ii), etale-local comparison paragraph: compatibility of projection mates with normalized etale comparisons

proof.text: Since $(*)$ is equivalent to the square by step 2 (the co-projections being the inverses of the $\kappa$'s and $\mu_e,\mu_v$ isomorphisms), the square commutes. The invertibility of the five arrows of $B_{e,i,K}$ used in step 1 comes from [lem-sf-mate] and [thm-sf-comp-composition] for $c_{e,i_U},c_{i,v}$ [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition] and from [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization] for $\rho_e,\rho_v$. The calculation is natural in $K$ and in the tensor-invertible $L$, so it applies in particular to $L=\Lambda(c)[2c]$ and to each component dimension. Every comparison used is one of the specified canonical maps, so the conclusion concerns the chosen co-projection isomorphisms and normalized $\rho$ comparisons, not an unspecified isomorphism.
